panels.visual: The sanctuary of Asclepius at Epidaurus: marble temples among pines, sick people arriving on mules and carried on stretchers
panels.caption: Epidaurus was the most famous sanctuary of Asclepius, the god of healing.

panels.visual: A long hall with rows of beds where patients sleep, moonlight, a faint dream bubble of a robed god with a staff
panels.caption: They slept in a special hall, hoping the god would visit them in a dream.

panels.visual: Harmless little snakes slithering around the sanctuary floor, children leaning out in fear and wonder, Glauka watching
panels.caption: Harmless snakes slithered around the sanctuary.

panels.visual: A snake coiled round a staff, the symbol of medicine, and a stone tablet with writing: priests chiselling a list of cures
panels.caption: The snake on a staff is still the symbol of medicine. Stone tablets list the cures people claimed.
